Largest county jail system in the US. Multiple facilities.

Finding information about an inmate in Los Angeles County jails is easier than you might think. Whether you need to locate a family member, friend, or just need information about someone in custody, the Los Angeles County California inmate lookup system provides public access to booking records and inmate details. Los Angeles County operates one of the largest jail systems in the United States, with multiple facilities housing thousands of individuals awaiting trial or serving sentences.

How to Search Los Angeles County Jail Records

  1. Visit the official Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department inmate search portal at app4.lasd.org or use the direct link to their inmate details system. This is the fastest and most reliable way to search.
  2. Enter the inmate's full name, last name, or booking number if you have it. The system will search all Los Angeles County detention facilities.
  3. Review the search results, which typically display the inmate's name, booking date, charges, and current facility location.
  4. Click on the inmate's record to view additional details such as bail amount, next court date, and charges filed.
  5. If the inmate is not found in the county system, check the California Department of Corrections website for inmates in state prison or the Federal Bureau of Prisons locator if they are in federal custody.

Bail Bond Information for Los Angeles County

If someone you know has been arrested in Los Angeles County, understanding bail and bond options is crucial. The bail amount is typically set at the suspect's first appearance or arraignment hearing. A professional bail bondsman can help secure the inmate's release by posting a bond with the court. Most bail bond companies charge a non-refundable fee of approximately 10% of the total bail amount. For example, if bail is set at $10,000, a bondsman's fee would be around $1,000. This fee is standard across California and is regulated by the state insurance commissioner.

The arraignment process in Los Angeles County typically occurs within 72 hours of arrest (excluding weekends and holidays). During this hearing, the judge reviews the charges, sets bail, and the defendant has the right to have an attorney appointed if they cannot afford one. If you need a bail bond, numerous licensed bondsmen operate throughout Los Angeles County and can often process paperwork quickly. It's important to work with a reputable, licensed bail bond company to avoid scams. Many facilities also accept direct bail payments, though this process is slower than using a bondsman.

Visitation Rules at Los Angeles County Jail

  • Photo ID Required: All visitors must present a valid government-issued photo identification, such as a driver's license or passport, to enter any Los Angeles County detention facility.
  • Visitation Hours: Most Los Angeles County facilities allow visits during specific hours, typically ranging from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays and Saturdays. Some facilities may have different schedules, so confirm hours before visiting.
  • Dress Code: Visitors must dress modestly and appropriately. Clothing that is revealing, gang-affiliated, or distracting is prohibited. Avoid wearing all red or all blue, as these colors are associated with gang affiliations.
  • Video Visits: Many Los Angeles County jails now offer video visitation services, allowing family members to connect remotely through secure video platforms. This option is especially useful for those unable to visit in person.
  • Children: Children under 18 may visit but must be supervised by an adult at all times. Some facilities have restrictions on the number of children per visit or require advance notice when bringing minors.

What to Expect After Arrest in Los Angeles County

  1. Booking: After arrest, the suspect is taken to a local Los Angeles County Sheriff's station or the main Men's Central Jail or Women's Central Jail for booking. During this process, personal information is recorded, photographs and fingerprints are taken, and a background check is conducted.
  2. Medical Screening: A nurse or medical professional conducts a health screening to identify any immediate medical needs or infectious diseases. Inmates with serious medical conditions may be transferred to specialized facilities.
  3. Classification: Staff classify the inmate based on their charges, criminal history, behavior, and other factors to determine which facility is most appropriate and what security level they require.
  4. Arraignment Hearing: Within 72 hours of arrest, the inmate must appear before a judge for their initial appearance (arraignment). At this hearing, charges are read, bail is set, and the defendant can request a public defender.
  5. Transfer: Depending on bail decisions and case status, the inmate may be released, held pending trial, or transferred to a longer-term facility or state prison.

How to Contact Los Angeles County Jail

For questions about an inmate, visitation, bail information, or general inquiries about Los Angeles County detention facilities, you can contact the Sheriff's Department directly. The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department operates multiple facilities and maintains phone lines for public inquiries during business hours. Having the inmate's full name and booking number will help staff locate information quickly.

Frequently Asked Questions — Los Angeles County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Los Angeles County jail?

The easiest way is to use the official Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department inmate search system at app4.lasd.org/iic/ajis_inmate_details.cfm. You can search by the inmate's name or booking number. The system is available online 24/7 and provides real-time information about inmates in county custody.

How long does booking take in Los Angeles County?

The booking process typically takes 2 to 8 hours, depending on the facility's workload and the complexity of the case. During peak times, booking may take longer. Once booking is complete, the inmate's information will appear in the searchable system.

Can I visit an inmate at Los Angeles County jail?

Yes, you can visit inmates at most Los Angeles County detention facilities during designated visitation hours. You must bring a valid government-issued photo ID, follow the dress code, and check with the specific facility for their visitation schedule, as hours vary by location.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

If someone is not in Los Angeles County jails, they may be in a different county facility, state prison, or federal custody. Check the California Department of Corrections website or the Federal Bureau of Prisons inmate locator. You can also contact local law enforcement to ask where the person is being held.

How do I send money to an inmate in Los Angeles County?

Los Angeles County jails accept deposits through multiple methods, including phone, online portals, and in-person at certain facilities. Funds are typically available to the inmate within a few hours to one business day. Contact the specific facility or use the Sheriff's Department website for instructions on depositing money.
